title: "Software"
---

```{r}
#| include: false
source(file.path(Sys.getenv("QUARTO_PROJECT_DIR", "."), "R", "site.R"))
proj <- site_links()
proj <- proj[proj$group == "projects", ]
links <- setNames(proj$url, proj$label)

# Downstream work, keyed by the software_dev name it came out of. The
# generated data has no field for this, so the mapping is kept here. The
# descriptions themselves are escaped with md() and so cannot carry a link,
# which is why this is a button rather than a sentence.
# The id is the links.yml entry; the value is the button label, which says who
# did the port, since beside "Source on GitHub" a bare name reads as if this
# tool had moved there.
related <- list("Table Relationship Explorer" = c(cartographer = "Cartographer, ported by Common Gene Labs"))
```

I build R and Shiny tools for the unglamorous middle of applied research: documenting, cleaning, linking, and reporting on administrative data.

```{r}
#| results: asis
d <- cv_data("software_dev")
# software_dev is generated, so a rename upstream would otherwise pass silently:
# a public tool would be labelled "Internal tool" and a downstream button would
# vanish. Both are matched by name, so both fail the render instead.
gone <- setdiff(c(proj$label, names(related)), d$name)
if (length(gone)) {
  stop("software_dev has no entry named ", paste0("'", gone, "'", collapse = ", "),
       ". If the export renamed it, change the label in links.yml's `projects` group,",
       " or the name in `related` in software.qmd, to match.", call. = FALSE)
}
for (i in seq_len(nrow(d))) {
  cat("## ", md(d$name[i]), "\n\n", sep = "")
  cat("*", md(d$role[i]), " · ", md(d$when[i]), "*\n\n", sep = "")
  cat(md(d$description[i]), "\n\n", sep = "")
  if (d$name[i] %in% names(links)) {
    btn <- paste0("[Source on GitHub](", links[[d$name[i]]],
                  "){.btn .btn-outline-primary .btn-sm}")
  } else {
    btn <- "*Internal tool; not publicly available.*"
  }
  rel <- related[[d$name[i]]]
  for (k in seq_along(rel)) {
    btn <- c(btn, paste0(link(names(rel)[k], rel[[k]]),
                         "{.btn .btn-outline-secondary .btn-sm}"))
  }
  # One line, so the buttons sit in a row rather than stacking as paragraphs.
  cat(paste(btn, collapse = " "), "\n\n", sep = "")
}
```
